submission.natural_language_explanation: The positive pole fires on the possessive 'at' phrase of terms and prerogative - 'at' + your/its/their + (own/sole) + a noun naming what is left to a party or at stake for it ('at your option' 14.5, 'at its sole discretion' 25.7, 'at their option' 16.2, 'at your own risk' 23.3, 'at your earliest convenience' 8.1, and the modal permission 'you may use the software at your home' 15.1) - and on the copyright-licence formula 'Use of this/these <thing> is ...' ('Use of this source code is governed by ...' 11.3). It peaks on the possessive determiner itself or on the 'at' immediately before it and its output finishes the phrase ('at'->'your', 'your'->'own', 'its'->'sole'; ablating it shifts probability onto ' own', ' option', ' risk', ' sole'), while it stays near zero on locative or temporal 'at' without a possessive ('at the station' 0.4, 'at 37 C' 0.0, 'at noon' 0.0, 'at 3 percent' 1.3, 'at 60 mph' 0.1), on 'at + possessive' inside plain event narration ('we stayed at your house' 0.2, 'she looked at your picture' 0.3, 'the parties met at their office' 1.0), on a third-person possessive in a stative location ('the book is at his home' 1.1, 'at its home' 0.4, 'at the home' 0.2), and on licence wording outside those formulae ('Permission is hereby granted' 0.7, 'IN NO EVENT SHALL' 0.4, 'This software is licensed under' 0.5, 'You may not use this file except in compliance' 2.7).

[A meningioma in the posterior fossa without dural attachment: case report].
An extremely rare case of a meningioma in the posterior fossa without dural attachment has been reported. The patient was a 56-year-old male whose chief manifestation was the abnormality of his CT scan. His past history included gastric and colonic polyp when he was 54, 55 years old, and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma before hospitalization in our department. CT scan showed a small round non-enhancing lesion located at the lateral site of the right cerebellar cortex. T1 weighted image of MRI showed a homogeneous low intensity lesion with partial enhancing with Gd-DTPA. Proton image showed a remarkable low intensity lesion which showed an extramedullary mass. Right retromastoid craniectomy was performed. The mass was an extramedullary tumor which had no relation with the cerebellar cortex and dura matter. The arachnoid membrane around the tumor was intact. The tumor was totally resected and the patient had no neurological deficits. Histopathologically, the tumor was delineated into laminar structures by collagen fiber. Tumor cells were spindle in shape and made a whorling formation. There was no psammoma body and it had a hyperchromatic nuclei without mitotic features. Electron microscopic studies revealed no typical interdigitation but irregularity of the cell membrane. Abundant collagen fibers were in contact with basement membrane of the tumor. According to these findings, we diagnosed fibroblastic meningioma with atypical forms. Meningiomas without dural attachment are rare in adults, especially extremely rare of the posterior fossa. There are only 23 previous reports of "meningioma of the posterior fossa without dural attachment". Cantore divided these meningiomas into three groups (IV ventricle, inferior tela choroidea and cisterna magna).(ABSTRACT TRUNCATED AT 250 WORDS)

a script that will do a 
SET GLOBAL SQL_SLAVE_SKIP_COUNTER = 1;

for every query that produces and error ?

A:

If you really don't care about that table, you can use pt-slave-restart on the slave and have it skip those problems.  I would be conservative about running it and make sure that you are only skipping queries for the table/database that you don't care about or at least for only a specific error.
You didn't post what the error code was in the output from SHOW SLAVE STATUS, but I suspect it is error 1146.
For example, this will skip all errors for 1146:
pt-slave-restart -u root -p pass --error-numbers 1146

Or, you could try skipping all errors that reference that table
pt-slave-restart -u root -p pass --error-text 'database2'

Another way to do this would be to set replicate-ignore-db=database2 and restart MySQL on the slave, but there are some caveats to how that works that you should read about in the documentation

A:

I think the bigger problem here is your default database context was database1.  Thats's why  your slave tried to execute the update on database2 since it was specified in database2.table format.
Basically it's not safe to user db.table syntax with wildcards or you find yourself in the situation you did.  If you're wanting to use the wildcard do or ignores it's generally safer to always specify your default db using "use" and execute the query in that context.

namespace Doctrine\ORM\Internal\Hydration;

use Doctrine\DBAL\Connection;

/**
 * Hydrator that produces flat, rectangular results of scalar data.
 * The created result is almost the same as a regular SQL result set, except
 * that column names are mapped to field names and data type conversions take place.
 *
 * @author Roman Borschel <roman@code-factory.org>
 * @since 2.0
 */
class ScalarHydrator extends AbstractHydrator
{
    /** @override */
    protected function _hydrateAll()
    {
        $result = array();
        $cache = array();
        while ($data = $this->_stmt->fetch(\PDO::FETCH_ASSOC)) {
            $result[] = $this->_gatherScalarRowData($data, $cache);
        }
        return $result;
    }

    /** @override */
    protected function _hydrateRow(array $data, array &$cache, array &$result)
    {
        $result[] = $this->_gatherScalarRowData($data, $cache);
    }
}

Neighbors (novel)

Neighbors is a 1980 novel by American author Thomas Berger. It is a satire of manners and suburbia, and a comment on emotional alienation with echoes of the works of Franz Kafka. Earl Keese’s character and situation begin realistically but become increasingly fantastic. Keese is an Everyman whose life is swiftly turned upside down. As he scrambles to reclaim his sense of normalcy and dignity, he comes to think that everyone, including his family, is against him.

Plot summary 

Earl Keese is a middle-aged, middle-class suburbanite with a wife, Enid, and teenage daughter, Elaine. Earl is content with his dull, unexceptional life, but this changes when a younger, less sophisticated couple, Harry and Ramona, move in next door. Harry is physically intimidating and vulgar; Ramona is sexually aggressive, and both impose themselves on the Keese household. Their free-spirited personalities and overbearing and boorish behavior endear them to Enid and Elaine, but Earl fears that he is losing control of his life and his family. Over the course of one night, the antagonism between Earl and his new neighbors escalates into suburban warfare.

Analysis 
Berger's off-kilter tone blurs the line between paranoia and reality, defense and offense, action and intention, ally and adversary. Harry and Ramona seem to constantly undergo changes in their respective personalities and Enid and Elaine appear to choose sides against Earl at random, but Berger also implies that it is Earl’s sense of reality that is skewed and deluded.

Earl is frustrated because he can never prove that Harry and Ramona are doing anything wrong on purpose, and the more he attempts to expose them, the more ridiculous he makes himself. Yet Earl comes to realize that Harry and Ramona have served as the crucible of his redemption: being forced out of his comfort zone of complacency and habit has provided him with an excitement he has never known before. As Earl comes to recognize value in his neighbors, he realizes that his wife is a distrustful alcoholic, his daughter is an underachiever and petty thief, and that his new neighbors can provide him with an escape from his existence of insignificance and emotional impotence. From a nightmare comes hope and a strengthened resolve to survive. adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The trail crew has finished its autumn work on the northern section of the Kettle Ridge loop, and walkers will notice several changes this season. The old boardwalk over the marshy stretch near mile three has been replaced with a raised gravel path, and two new signs have gone up at the junction where the loop meets the fire road. Rangers say the work should reduce erosion and keep walkers out of the wettest ground during the spring melt.

The upper ridge is a different matter. The final mile and a half climbs steeply over loose scree, and the service has decided not to install railings or a maintained path there. "We looked at the cost of a permanent walkway, and it was simply not something we could justify for a route that sees maybe two hundred people a year," said district supervisor Ellen Marsh. "People who want the view from the top should understand what they are getting into."

The decision follows two rescues last autumn, one of which involved a visitor from Ohio who lost the route in fog and spent the night beside a cairn. The service has published a short guide describing the scramble, the exposure near the summit block, and the usual weather pattern in the shoulder season. Rangers have also begun recording how many people sign the log at the lower trailhead, although the figures are rough because many walkers ignore it.

Local walking groups have welcomed the clarity. "For years people assumed the ridge was maintained because the lower loop is," said Priya Raman, who leads a fortnightly hiking club from the village. "Nobody is telling anyone to stay away. The point is that the decision belongs to the person on the ground, and the sign says so plainly." She added that her group will keep running the lower loop on Wednesday evenings and will offer a guided ascent once a month during the summer, with a leader who knows the route.

The service has now posted a notice at each trailhead stating that the upper ridge is unmarked and unpatrolled, that there is no cell coverage beyond the saddle, and that hikers continue at their own risk. The wording was agreed with the county attorney, who asked for the exposure and the lack of coverage to be spelled out separately. The service plans to review the arrangement after two seasons, and may add a rope section on the steepest pitch if accident reports justify it.

For now, the gravel path, the new signs and the printed guide are the whole of the investment. Rangers ask walkers to carry water, to start early, and to turn back if the cloud base drops below the summit block. The car park at the trailhead closes at dusk, and overnight camping is not permitted anywhere on the ridge.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Moving house is usually described as one of the most stressful events in ordinary life, and most of the difficulty comes from the week before the van arrives rather than the day itself. A little planning goes a long way. Start by clearing the loft and the cupboards you never open, because every box you do not pack is a box somebody else has to carry down a staircase.

Two weeks out, book the van and confirm the time in writing. Removal firms often give a window rather than a fixed hour, and the difference between nine and eleven can decide whether you are unloading in daylight. Label each box by room, not by contents. On the day itself, keep a separate bag with chargers, medication, a change of clothes and the kettle, and leave it at your feet in the cab so that it does not disappear into the pile.

Tell the utility companies the date you are leaving and the date you arrive. Meter readings taken on the morning of the move will save an argument later. If you are renting, photograph every room before you hand back the keys, including the inside of the oven and any marks on the walls. The deposit is easier to recover when there is a record of how the place looked when you arrived.

Families with children should visit the new area before the move if they can. Walking past the school gates and the local park helps more than any conversation. Once you have registered the children at their school, ask about the bus route and the collection point, because the first week is confusing enough without an unexpected walk. If you work from home, set up a chair and a lamp at your desk before you unpack anything else; a usable corner makes the rest of the house feel less overwhelming.

The letting agent will usually meet you at the flat on the morning of the handover. Read the inventory before you sign it, and check that the keys you have been given open the back door as well as the front. Keep the agent's number somewhere you can find it without unpacking. If the previous tenants left furniture behind, agree in writing whether it stays or goes, and photograph it either way.

Finally, accept that the first fortnight will be chaotic. The boxes will sit in the hallway longer than you expect, and something essential will be missing. Ordering a takeaway on the first night is not a failure of planning. Most people find that the new place begins to feel like home somewhere in the second month, once the pictures are up and the route to the shops has become routine. Invite a neighbour for coffee before the last box is unpacked; it is the quickest way to stop the flat feeling like a storage unit.
